    About this tree & interviews

    About this tree

    The Andreoni · Mazzaccaro · Azzolini family tree: 685 people and 449 sources across 34 family lines. It was started from an interview with Norma (Mazzaccaro) Azzolini and is extended daily from public records and obituaries. Documented records win over interview memory; where they disagree, both are shown as a conflict.

    Download GEDCOM (family-tree.ged) living people masked

    Interviews

    What was told by family, who told it, and when. Each interview fact in the tree is tagged Interview and cites one of these sessions.

      Interview context

      Stories and narrative from Norma’s interview (moves and schools, Doc’s career, the deli and Pinnacle Supermarket, Navy, Philomena, golf, the house-moving story, Alice’s stories) are kept in a separate document, not on this page. The shared Google Doc is linked below.

      Open the interview context document

      Privacy

      No addresses, contact details or identification numbers are recorded. Living people show names and relationships only: no dates, places or photos. Interview narrative is not published here.

      Research notes & open questions

      Open questions are conflicts between sources and records searched for but not found. This page lists the people they affect, plus conclusions the tree makes that no record states directly. Open a person’s Notes tab for the detail.

      Conflicts & open questions

      • Parodi Cigar Factory location — Tim: Baltimore. Find a Grave bio: Scranton. Company histories place Parodi’s Scranton plant from 1930; no Baltimore plant found. If Angelina rolled cigars for Parodi it was most likely in Scranton after 1930. Baltimore is where she died. [7] [14] [15] [16]
      • Giovanni’s birthplace — Tim: Perugia region. Records found: “Italy” only (SSA Numident abstract). Not a contradiction, but unverified. Context: son-in-law Giuseppe Incociati was born in Perugia; the Biscontini surname clusters in the Province of Perugia. [2] [8] [9]
      • “Gussie” = Louis J. Guzzi? — Tim: Irma married “Gussie”. Records: Irma’s husband was Louis J. Guzzi (1894–1978). “Gussie” is likely a nickname from the surname (Assumed, likely). [6] [61]
      • Eva’s surname — Wittick (Tim) / Winnick (first heard) vs Widdick (SSA, Find a Grave, Baltimore Sun). [91] [4]
      • Tim’s “Luis → Olga, Eva” recollection — Olga and Eva are records-proven daughters of Giovanni and Angelina (Alice’s sisters). Eva Widdick’s 2005 obituary names daughters Angela Rose, Frances Widdick, Linda Smith and Maria Brauer — matching Tim’s four daughters. Daughters placed under Eva Widdick; sisters not moved; “Luis” kept as a flagged note (possibly Louis J. Guzzi). [91] [61]
      • Marie vs Maria — Tim: Marie. Obituary: Maria Brauer. [91]
      • Olga’s surname — Oberholzer (heard) vs Oberholtzer (records). [86] [3]
      • Rigo/Rico vs Merico “Rego” — Same person; record given name Merico, nickname Rego. [58]
      • Dora’s birth year — 1901 (Find a Grave family lists) vs 1909 (SSA death index entry for Dora Barbetti, Old Forge). The 1950 census (age 40) supports about 1909–10. [18] [19] [22]
      • Irma’s death place and birth date — Find a Grave: died Lackawanna Co., Pa. Death index: Maryland. Birth 14 Aug 1913 vs 14 Apr 1912 in a second index entry. [6] [62]
      • Mary Lero vs Mary Ann Lerro — Tim spells Lero; records spell Lerro. Birth 11 Jun (Find a Grave) vs 13 Jun 1915 (SSA). [118] [72]
      • Louise Aulisio — Tim says Thomas’s sister was Mary Lero, not Louise Alessio/Aulisio. Records (father’s Find a Grave children list; mother’s 1957 obituary “Mrs. Dominick Aulisio, Newark”) indicate Louise was also a sister. Shown as possible additional sibling, unconfirmed by family. [71] [105] [122]
      • Patrick Joseph “Papp” — Tim: Patrick Joseph Papp, married Mary Febbo. Assumed to be Patrick Joseph Mazzaccaro (1920–1968), whose wife was Mary Febbo. [126] [127]
      • Pat Jr. — Family: possible child, unconfirmed. Records: Mary Febbo’s obituary names Patrick Mazzaccaro Jr. as her late son. [127] [128]
      • Surname spelling Mazzacaro / Mazzaccaro / Mazzacarro / Mazzucaro — Family usage Mazzacaro; records overwhelmingly Mazzaccaro (double c); Alice’s obituary has “Mazzacarro”; Alice’s memorial spells her maiden name “Anderoni”. [70] [68] [67]
      • “AMP” vs A&P — Norma said Doc was a supervisor at “AMP”; his obituary says A&P. [74]
      • Dominic vs Dominick; Tonyann vs Toni Ann; Lindsey vs Lyndsey — Interview spellings differ from Doc’s 2024 obituary. [74]
      • Deli story / which Anthony — Who died during the deli period and whether the “Anthony” is son Anthony T. (d. 1995) is unresolved. Details in the interview-context document. [1]
      • John Mazzaccaro’s birthplace — Find a Grave gives “Castel, Provincia di Aosta” — implausible for a southern-Italian surname; treated as Italy only. [71]
      • Dominick and Sandy Roy Barbetti birth dates — Dominick: 15 Apr 1911 (Find a Grave) vs 20 Apr 1911 (SSA death index). Sandy Roy: 19 Jun 1916 (Find a Grave) vs 19 Jun 1915 (SSA death index). Tree keeps Find a Grave. [274] [292] [277] [19]
      • David Barbetti’s parentage — Henrietta Barbetti’s 2010 obituary lists grandson David Barbetti; Jacqueline Barbetti’s 2025 obituary lists only children Joseph, Deborah and Donna. Placed under Joseph L. Barbetti provisionally. [275] [279]
      • Lucrezia’s maiden name: DiNicolo vs De Nichilo — Family/obituaries and Tim (9 Nov 2026): DiNicolo. 1938 SS Rex passenger index: “Lucrezia De Nichilo”, 31, on the same page as her sons; De Nichilo is also the commonest form of the surname in Molfetta. Tree keeps DiNicolo; De Nichilo recorded as the likely Italian spelling. [79] [135] [77] [1]
      • Azzolini arrival year: 1938 vs 1939 — Patsy’s obituary: 1939, with Patrick 9 and Dominick 6. Passenger index: SS Rex, 1938, Pasquale 8 and Domenico 5 (fits late 1938). Same index gives Domenico’s birthplace as “U S A” (obituary: Molfetta; 1950 census: Italy) — probably an indexing slip. [79] [76] [78]
      • Lena Dello Russo’s birth date — 23 Mar 1927 (funeral-home obituary) vs 27 Mar 1927 (Find a Grave). Tree keeps 23 Mar. [437] [438]
      • Anthony F. DeMarco’s birthplace and death date — Find a Grave: born Medford, died 27 Sep 2002. His 2002 obituary: “born and raised in Boston”, died on a Thursday with the funeral Monday 30 Sep (so Thu 26 Sep 2002). Tree keeps Find a Grave. [432] [433]
      • Joe Costa Sr.’s birthplace in the Azores — Find a Grave: “Picao, Vila da Praia da Vitória” (Terceira island). His son John’s 2017 obituary: the family emigrated from Pico Island in 1910. Tree records Azores, Portugal only. [439] [440]
      • Sabino and Pamela DeMarco’s ages in the 1950 census — Census (West Roxbury, April 1950): “Samuel” DeMarco 42 and Pamela 9. Find a Grave: Sabino born 1 Sep 1905 (44) and Pamela born 24 May 1941 (8). Tree keeps Find a Grave dates. [384] [405] [394]
      • Tenerelli vs Teneriello — Mary Comperchio’s husband: Tenerelli (her memorial and daughters’ obituaries) vs Teneriello (his Find a Grave memorial). [414] [415]
      • Sibling count — Earlier tree draft showed 9 / Tim expected 7. With Gussie removed (he was Irma’s husband), the interview list has 8 children of Giovanni and Angelina, matching the 8 in records. [6] [1]
      • Helen (Regan) Cronin’s death date and place — SSA abstract and Find a Grave: 25 Apr 1996; Find a Grave places the death in Norwood. A death-notice index lists 26 Apr 1996 “in West Roxbury” (Boston Globe, 27 Apr 1996). Tree keeps 25 Apr 1996 and records Massachusetts only. [385] [381] [386]
      • Mary (O’Brien) Regan’s middle name — Helen Cronin’s SSA abstract and Watkins Patrick Regan’s Find a Grave bio: Mary M. O’Brien. Her own Find a Grave memorial: Mary Ann O’Brien Regan. Tree keeps “Mary M.” and lists Mary Ann as a variant. [385] [402] [404]
      • Who Grandpa Cronin’s parents are — Tim: Tim Cronin and Helen Regan. Records: Timothy Henry Cronin (1895–1947) and Helen Louise Regan (1907–1996) married in 1938 and share a grave in West Roxbury. No record yet names Grandpa as their son, so the link is shown as likely, not confirmed. [380] [375] [381]

      Data standards used

      • Names: Given names then SURNAME; women are recorded under their birth (maiden) surname with married surnames listed separately (GEDCOM NAME “Given /Surname/”, with married names as an additional NAME of TYPE married). Family-used names (“Mary Lero”, “Eva Wittick”) are shown as the card label, with record spellings and variants listed on the card.
      • Dates: DD Mon YYYY (e.g. 30 May 1877); qualifiers ABT (about), BEF (before), AFT (after), BET … AND … as in GEDCOM 5.5.1. Partial dates kept as given (1880, Aug 1978).
      • Places: Smallest to largest, comma-separated: City, County, State, Country (e.g. Old Forge, Lackawanna, Pennsylvania, USA). Unknown levels are omitted.
      • IDs: Every person has a stable unique ID (I = Andreoni side, M = Mazzaccaro, A = Azzolini, N = Norma’s generation, C = Norma’s children, G = grandchildren). The same IDs are used as @I…@ record IDs in family-tree.ged.
      • Citations: Each assertion is tied to its own source (Evidence Explained principle: cite each individual assertion to its own source). Sources are numbered in the Sources list with title, repository/website and URL.
      • Evidence tags: Interview = told by Norma via Tim; Record = found in a public record or record abstract (with link); Assumed = a researcher inference; Conflict = sources disagree — both sides shown, conflict stated, and the preferred reading explained (BCG Genealogy Standards: conflicting evidence is shown, not hidden).
      • Confidence: confirmed (direct, consistent records), likely (secondary or user-contributed sources that agree), unconfirmed (single, indirect, or family-only). Maps to GEDCOM QUAY 3 / 2 / 1.
      • Living people: Possibly-living people show names and relationships only (no dates or places), and are exported to GEDCOM as “Living” with no details (FamilySearch privacy guidance). No addresses, contact details, or identification numbers.
      • Photos: Photos are small thumbnails (max 320 px) of images already published on public pages (Find a Grave memorial photos, which are user-contributed, and funeral-home or newspaper obituaries), shown with attribution, a link to the source page and a confidence level (confirmed = captioned with the name or an obituary photo; likely = an uncaptioned photo on the person’s own memorial). Copyrights remain with their owners (the contributors, families, funeral homes and newspapers); the photos are used here for private family research and can be removed on request. No placeholder, stock image or silhouette is used: where none was found the card says so and lists what was searched. Living people: no photo was sought.
      • Chart: Descendant (drop-line) charts: one chart per ancestral line, oldest generation at top, children in birth order left-to-right where known, spouses side by side joined by ⚭, double-surname lines linked across charts.

      Best-practice references:

      • GEDCOM 5.5.1 specification (FamilySearch, gedcom.io)
      • FamilySearch GEDCOM 7 specification
      • Evidence Explained: “Multiple Citations for Individual Elements”
      • Evidence Explained QuickTip: proof arguments & citing ourselves in the process
      • Board for Certification of Genealogists: Skillbuilding — Proof Arguments
      • WAGS 2026 handout on conflicting evidence (applying BCG Genealogy Standards)
      • FamilySearch: Add living relatives (privacy guidance)
      • FamilySearch: Contributing to Family Tree (standardized dates/places, show conflicts)
